Short answer: you need formal R&S product/specification evidence, formal competitor evidence, and AI-specific validation evidence; current battle cards and AI-server sales mappings are not enough for customer-facing comparison claims.[4][49][56]
- Use formal R&S specifications / features documents for Signaling Tester claims, because the CMX500 page separates binding specifications from non-binding feature overview data, and says data without tolerance limits is not binding.[33]
- Use CMX500 specs/features only for the exact supported capabilities they state, such as LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, TDD, signaling, WLAN signaling, fading, throughput measurement, application testing, XLAPI and SCPI control.[30][31]
- Use formal option evidence for signaling scope, such as listed CMX500 NR signaling, RedCap, NTN, NB-NTN, WLAN and LTE signaling option codes and dependencies.[32][34][37]
- Use separate formal specifications for any Non-signaling / production tester claim, because the battle-card production path to CMP180, CMP200 and CMW100 K06 is only sales positioning unless each production platform is backed by its own formal source.[22][60]
- Do not use the AI server ecosystem mapping as proof of a formal configuration, customer fit, opportunity, or validated test setup, because its R&S Solution column is not a datasheet, application note, configuration guide or ordering guide.[2][4]
- For competitor claims, obtain competitor official datasheets, feature documents, option / order guides, release status, and test conditions, because the Keysight comparison currently comes from an R&S internal battle card and needs Keysight official or third-party evidence for customer documents.[39][56]
- Do not present “only platform,” “first validated,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” or “fewer boxes” as technical facts, because these are identified as sales language rather than verifiable specifications.[56]
- For AI-specific comparison, obtain formal AI Script Assistant product version, software release, order number, license code, support matrix, deployment details, supported CMX500 software release, XLAPI version, Python version, script packages, 3GPP release coverage, application test scope, validation method, human review workflow, error handling, security / data residency / IP handling, and model-update governance, because the current AI Script Assistant source does not provide them.[49]
- Do not claim AI performance superiority without benchmark, correctness metric, coverage matrix, supported script package list, or validation conditions, because the current source does not provide those.[50]
- Do not claim deployment model such as cloud, on-prem, hybrid, or air-gapped unless a source states it, because “various deployment options” is not expanded.[52]
- Any comparison table should cite R&S formal specs for R&S capabilities and competitor official / third-party sources for competitor capabilities; battle cards may only be labeled as sales positioning, not independent technical proof.[16][56]

- **Unified Automation**：將 CMsquares、CMsequencer、CONTEST、AI Script Assistant 定位為 one unified environment；對比 Atlas、Channel Studio、RaySim、WLAN-specific tools、Nemo、UXM-specific application features。

Short answer: you need formal R&S product/specification evidence, formal competitor evidence, and AI-specific validation evidence; current battle cards and AI-server sales mappings are not enough for customer-facing comparison claims.[4][49][56]
- Use formal R&S specifications / features documents for Signaling Tester claims, because the CMX500 page separates binding specifications from non-binding feature overview data, and says data without tolerance limits is not binding.[33]
- Use CMX500 specs/features only for the exact supported capabilities they state, such as LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, TDD, signaling, WLAN signaling, fading, throughput measurement, application testing, XLAPI and SCPI control.[30][31]
- Use formal option evidence for signaling scope, such as listed CMX500 NR signaling, RedCap, NTN, NB-NTN, WLAN and LTE signaling option codes and dependencies.[32][34][37]
- Use separate formal specifications for any Non-signaling / production tester claim, because the battle-card production path to CMP180, CMP200 and CMW100 K06 is only sales positioning unless each production platform is backed by its own formal source.[22][60]
- Do not use the AI server ecosystem mapping as proof of a formal configuration, customer fit, opportunity, or validated test setup, because its R&S Solution column is not a datasheet, application note, configuration guide or ordering guide.[2][4]
- For competitor claims, obtain competitor official datasheets, feature documents, option / order guides, release status, and test conditions, because the Keysight comparison currently comes from an R&S internal battle card and needs Keysight official or third-party evidence for customer documents.[39][56]
- Do not present “only platform,” “first validated,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” or “fewer boxes” as technical facts, because these are identified as sales language rather than verifiable specifications.[56]
- For AI-specific comparison, obtain formal AI Script Assistant product version, software release, order number, license code, support matrix, deployment details, supported CMX500 software release, XLAPI version, Python version, script packages, 3GPP release coverage, application test scope, validation method, human review workflow, error handling, security / data residency / IP handling, and model-update governance, because the current AI Script Assistant source does not provide them.[49]
- Do not claim AI performance superiority without benchmark, correctness metric, coverage matrix, supported script package list, or validation conditions, because the current source does not provide those.[50]
- Do not claim deployment model such as cloud, on-prem, hybrid, or air-gapped unless a source states it, because “various deployment options” is not expanded.[52]
- Any comparison table should cite R&S formal specs for R&S capabilities and competitor official / third-party sources for competitor capabilities; battle cards may only be labeled as sales positioning, not independent technical proof.[16][56]
